formLanguage: bolted flange collars and gusseted base plates
objectClass.notes: A galvanised steel sign gantry: two 0.5 m box legs on gusseted base plates carrying a 5.2 x 1.75 m green direction board on two box rails, under a 7 m clearance. Nothing moves and nothing attaches: one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract. Every Bangkok expressway: a green direction board on a galvanised portal, the near leg carrying a maintenance ladder of staple rungs and a rust bloom under each bolted collar.

reasoning: TWO components on two materials: the galvanised frame (legs, cap plates, base plates, 8 tapered gussets, two 2-plate bolted collars with 16 bolts, two box rails, 4 rail end brackets, 6 hangers, 10 staple rungs on the LEFT leg's outer face only, and the rim lip around the board) merged into ONE geometry with height-keyed UVs; and the board tray, whose +Z face samples the plate's own rectified board through planar UVs.

Two materials of three: galvanised steel (white, vertex mud tint over the lowest 0.5 m, a height-keyed paint canvas for spangle, rust below the collars and the base grime) and the printed sheeting (white, the baked atlas as map). A third material was not needed: bolts, brackets and rungs differ from the legs only in tone and ride as vertex colours.

No repetition system: the rungs, bolts and gussets are 12-30 triangle boxes and cylinders, 1292 triangles in all against 8000, so a second draw call for an InstancedMesh would cost more than it saves. Action readiness: one root pivot at base-centre between the legs, zero sockets, one box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the portal itself -- two heavy box legs, the board hung between them on rails, the bolted collars, the gusseted feet and the rung ladder up one leg -- plus the printed face. The face is the plate's own pixels; the ironwork is measured off the plate crops and the proxy and built as real geometry rather than paint.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The board face is the plate's own rectified pixels (four corners into 5.2 x 1.75 m at 190 px/m); the plate's slight lens perspective across the near leg is absorbed by the rectification.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 6.70 x 7.00 x 0.80 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=3 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the portal envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry (two legs, the rails and the board).

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The board face is the plate's own rectified pixels (four corners into 5.2 x 1.75 m at 190 px/m); the plate's slight lens perspective across the near leg is absorbed by the rectification.
The rails are 0.25 m box sections at 6.5 and 5.7 m sitting 0.02 m inside the legs' front plane; the plate shows their end brackets in the gap beside the board but not their depth.
The right leg carries no rungs: the plate shows the ladder on the left leg only, and the right leg's outer face is clean.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: A 6.7 m wide, 7.0 m tall portal of two 0.5 m square legs on 0.85 m base plates, with a 5.2 x 1.75 m board filling the upper 1.75 m between them, its top level with the leg caps.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: 7.0 m tall as declared. The span is corrected 8.0 -> 6.7 m from the Meshy proxy, which reads the portal 0.95 H wide over the legs' outer faces (73 of 100 SIDE-map columns at 0.013 H each; 0.95 x 7.0 = 6.65 m); the plate is a three-quarter view that cannot give the span directly. Legs 0.5 m square (the plate's leg runs 40-63 px across two faces against a 742 px leg height, 0.085 of H over two faces = 0.42-0.5 m). The board is 0.24 H tall and 0.72 H wide in the proxy (rows 0.75-0.99, columns 14-86): 1.75 m tall with its top at 6.85 m, 5.2 m wide leaving 0.25 m to each leg, which the plate shows as the gap where the rail end brackets sit. The flange collars sit at the board's bottom edge (proxy bump at row 0.73 = 5.1 m; plate: the collar at y 390 is level with the board's lower corner). Base plates 0.85 x 0.75 m with 0.36 m gussets (proxy rows 0.01-0.05 H, 12 columns wide).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: The first build's Meshy proxy (scratch/expressway-gantry-sign/reference.glb) is the source of the span correction and the board rows; its SIDE map was read at 100 x 100 over 1.3 H x 1 H. The plate is a three-quarter elevation whose near leg is foreshortened, so the proxy governs proportion and the plate governs detail and tone.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the board's back is a plain grey tray on two box rails, which is what every gantry of this type shows from behind; the rails' depth is the one unobserved dimension.

componentTree.name: Galvanised portal
componentTree.topologyRationale: Legs, plates, gussets, collars, bolts, rails, brackets, hangers, rungs and the board lip merged on one material: the first draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Legs 0.5 sq at x +-3.1 to 7.0 m with 0.54 caps; base plates 0.85 x 0.75 x 0.03 with four 0.36 m tapered gussets each; two-plate collars 0.64 sq at 5.065 and 5.135 m with 8 bolts; rails 6.22 x 0.25 x 0.20 at 6.5 and 5.7 m, z 0.03..0.23; end brackets on the inner faces; 6 hangers to the tray; 10 rungs on the left leg's -X face; rim lip 0.035 wide round the board 0.005 into the tray.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Every plate stands proud of the face it sits on (caps 0.02 beyond the leg, collars 0.07, brackets 0.02 off the inner face, gussets on the faces); the rails end 0.01 inside each leg as interpenetration, not a shared plane; the lip starts 5 mm inside the tray front.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 7.0 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White galvanised material with a mud vertex tint over the foot and a height-keyed paint canvas for spangle, rust and grime.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the portal envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry (two legs, the rails and the board).

componentTree.name: Printed sign board
componentTree.topologyRationale: A 0.05 m tray on its own material because the face is a texture the galvanised canvas cannot carry: the second draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Rounded rectangle 5.2 x 1.75 m centred at 5.975 m, extruded z 0.27..0.32, hung on six 0.12 m stubs off the rails.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Its front is 0.02 m beyond the lip's front and its back is 0.04 m in front of the rails; the lip overlaps the tray edge as a ring 5 mm deep into it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One extrude; +Z vertices take planar atlas UVs.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White material; the +Z face samples the baked board atlas planarly, every other vertex pins to a grey back-tone strip.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/rightleg.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: under the collars at 4.85-5.05 m and the base plates
localOverrides.evidence: crops/collar.png -- rust bloom on the leg under the flange plates; crops/base.png -- grime and rust on the base plate and gussets.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-rightleg: the lit leg face reads #7e7e7e..#a0a2a4 (plate x 720-790, y 300-600, luma 130 mean) under a key that darkens the plate; authored as #c7ccd1 through a white material with a height-keyed paint canvas (base 0.78/0.80/0.82, chalk 0.90/0.92/0.93) that renders at the plate's luma under the harness key.

Rust bands: region-collar shows a rust bloom running 0.2 m under each collar and streaks below; the canvas carries an hband at 4.85-5.05 m (alpha 0.45, 80 specks) and 40 streaks from 4.85 m, plus a ground band (0.5) over the lowest 0.06 of the height and a vertex mud tint #b0a088 over the lowest 0.5 m (region-base).
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px paint canvas after construction, height-keyed over the whole 7.0 m so the rust sits under the collars once.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/board.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.900. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/board.png -- dust and streaking over the upper green field, carried by the plate pixels in the atlas.

evidence: The board IS the plate: its face is rectified from four solved corners -- (347,207) (733,100) (726,266) (351,391) -- into a 5.2 x 1.75 m plane at 190 px/m and baked as a 1007 x 332 WebP atlas (16 KB) that the tray's +Z face samples planarly; the Thai and Latin names, the 12 km, the white rule and the plate's grime arrive at their own positions.
The green field measures #2e6b4e..#3f6f5a on region-board; it is carried as the plate pixels with the corners rounded at 0.06 m, and the tray's other faces pin to a #b4b7b9 back-tone strip.
Textureless as DECLARED: the baked atlas is bound after construction, guarded for plain Node.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.90 and the six critical features 0.91. 1292/8000 triangles, 2/3 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/8 unique geometries, one 16 KB atlas and one 512 px canvas.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: galv and sheeting: 2 of 3; bolts, brackets and mud as vertex tints.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1292 of 8000: 52 boxes, 8 frusta, 16 six-sided bolts, two rounded extrudes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for the legs, plates, rails, brackets and rungs; frusta for the gussets; cylinders for the bolts; rounded-rectangle extrudes for the tray and its lip.
No InstancedMesh: the repeated parts total under 700 triangles, less than the draw call an instanced set would cost. A level instances whole gantries.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. One baked board atlas (16 KB WebP) and one 512 px paint canvas after construction, both guarded for plain Node.

risks.description: The 0.25 m gaps between the board's ends and the legs, divided by the two rails, enclose backdrop from the front and rear.
risks.mitigation: Real openings bounded by 0.25 m rails and 0.5 m legs: --allow-holes on the holeviz measurement (2182 px at 000, 2913 at 180 against a 1529 px 1% floor).

risks.description: The rails' depth and the tray back are unobserved.
risks.mitigation: Built to the type; recorded on region-back at 0.80.
